title: Tips for good world building with AI?
author: wewerecreaturres
selftext:
I’m a product manager by trade. I spend all day building software, but my expertise and creativity is in things like mechanics, good ui, etc, not creative artistry like building a good world. 

Has anyone here been able to build a nice world using ai? 

What do I mean by nice world? Realistic terrain. Logical rivers. Prefabs that aren’t floating. Good ground cover and texture and tree grouping and placement, etc.

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body: Procgen is a bit better at this—Houdini.

comments.author: GigaTerra
comments.body:
There is an lot of people who made good top down 2D levels for games like D&D, so if you want you can ask AI to generate an map from top down. Also ask it to generate an "screen shot of X game" will often give some good ideas, and you can ask it to visualize it like an blockout for design.

Screen shot level design: [https://imgur.com/a/QLhCQk4](https://imgur.com/a/QLhCQk4)

Top Down level design: [https://imgur.com/a/4vVUw2b](https://imgur.com/a/4vVUw2b)

replies.author: wewerecreaturres
replies.body: yeah im really looking to achieve something like the first link

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body:
You will have to build it, because like you will see the AI does make mistakes and over exaggerates, but it is an good guide, especially an fantastic tool for solving the blank canvas problem.

I am generating images like those, and then using Unity's Pro-builder and Blender to build levels for my game. Then I do the reverse, I take screenshots of my game and ask the AI to render it in styles so I can decide what to replace the objects with.

The assets I generate with 3D AI tools like Rodin AI. It ends up saving weeks to months when building levels for my game. Not to mention I am working to an higher standard than before.

replies.author: wewerecreaturres
replies.body: I started giving it "good" demo worlds to read and create rules from and that has helped, but not as much as id have liked unfortunately. may have to stick with games that are less outdoor world and more structural and ruled.
